value.body: Agricultural Engineering (B.Tech) applies engineering to farming: farm machinery and power, soil and water conservation, irrigation and drainage, post-harvest processing and renewable energy. It is offered mostly at state agricultural universities and some engineering colleges, and leads to work with farm-equipment makers, irrigation firms, agri-business and government agriculture bodies.

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Most seats are at state agricultural universities, which admit through a state CET (for example EAMCET, KCET or MHT-CET) or their own tests; a share of their seats is filled through ICAR counselling. Engineering colleges that offer the branch admit through JEE Main or state counselling. Class 12 with Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics is the usual requirement; some universities also admit students with Biology or Agriculture.

value.title: At a glance
items: Jobs are spread across tractor and farm-equipment makers, micro-irrigation firms, food processing and agri-input companies; many are field-based or in smaller towns.
Government routes include ICAR scientist posts (after a master's), NABARD, bank agriculture field officer posts and state agricultural engineering posts.
GATE has an Agricultural Engineering (AG) paper, used mainly for M.Tech admissions.
